summary: A read-through cache cut p99 render latency from 810ms to 120ms, at the cost of a week of wrong invalidation caused by an under-specified cache key.

product_facts.statement: A read-through cache was placed in front of the render pipeline in March 2026.
The cache key is built from document path, locale and publish revision, and non-200 responses are not cached.

development_history.summary: Profiling attributed 78% of wall time to the Markdown-to-AST step.
The cache shipped keyed on document path alone.
Locale and publish revision were added to the key and error responses excluded.

claims.text: p99 latency on article pages fell from 810ms to 120ms after the cache shipped.

evidence.quote: p99 latency fell from 810ms to 120ms on the article pages

claims.text: 78% of wall time was spent in the Markdown-to-AST step.

evidence.quote: Profiling showed 78% of wall time inside the Markdown-to-AST step

claims.text: Deterministic rendering is what makes caching viable rather than a source of stale bugs.
Readers on a non-default locale were served the English render for a week.

evidence.quote: readers on a non-default locale were served the English render

claims.text: The real mistake was treating invalidation as a follow-up task rather than part of the cache design.
Most teams shipping a cache under deadline make the same trade.

publication_constraints.description: The internal postmortem covering the deploy is not publishable.
publication_constraints.reason: The author marked it internal in the source.

lessons.statement: Design invalidation with the cache, not after it.
A cache key must name every input the render depends on.

potential_arguments.thesis: A cache key is a specification of what your render depends on, and getting it wrong is a correctness bug rather than a performance one.
Determinism is the precondition that makes caching a latency win instead of a staleness risk.
